title: Dijkstra's 'Go To Statement Considered Harmful' (1968)
explainer: Edsger Dijkstra's famous 1968 letter to Communications of the ACM argued that unrestricted goto statements make a program's runtime behavior too hard to trace from its source text, and it helped launch the shift toward structured programming built from functions, loops, and conditionals. That shift is a direct ancestor of the function- and module-based organization this lesson teaches: breaking code into small, well-scoped units specifically so behavior stays traceable from the code itself. Notably, Dijkstra did not choose the provocative title himself; an editor added it before publication.
